LESSON: TEMPERATURE AND THERMAL EXPANSION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: PHYSICS
Strand: Mechanics and Thermal Physics
Topic 1.4: Temperature and Thermal Expansion
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Temperature and Thermal Expansion, part of Mechanics and Thermal Physics in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 PHYSICS.

Key inquiry question: Why is the lid of a sufuria made wider? 2. Why does a glass bottle break when the water in it freezes?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Discuss with peers in groups the meaning of temperature and share findings. Learners with speech difficulties could be allowed more time to express themselves or they could use alternative communication modes as they hold discussions, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Discuss with peers in groups the meaning of temperature and share findings. Learners with speech difficulties could be allowed more time to express themselves or they could use alternative communication modes as they hold discussions, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Temperature and Thermal Expansion together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Citizenship: as the learner develops ethical digital citizenship skills when they search, access and use internet-based

services when searching for more information from the print or non-print media on the applications of thermal

expansion.

● Digital literacy: as the learner develops manipulative skills of interacting with digital technology when they use

digital technology to effectively accomplish their own tasks while searching for information from the digital media

on the applications of thermal expansion and measurement of temperature.

21

Values:
● Peace as the learner shows love by respecting diversity as they respect others and their opinions while discussing

applications of thermal expansion in day-to-day life.

● Patriotism: the learner shows dedication by being conscious of their social and moral duties as they carry out

activities to demonstrate thermal expansion and contraction in solids and determine linear expansivity of metals.

● Unity as learners take criticism positively.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Socio-economic and environmental issues: as the learner acquires safety and security skills by being keen on fire

safety while performing experiments to demonstrate thermal expansion and contraction in fluids.

22

Suggested assessment methods

● Oral /aural assessment

● Observation

● Written assessment

● Peer assessment

● Portfolio

● Individual assessment

● Teacher observations

Suggested learning resources

Adapted Digital devices, Internet, videos, liquid in glass thermometers, bimetallic strip, source of heat, test tubes,

thermocouple, glass bottle, coloured water, methylated spirit, kerosine, balloon, thermostat,
